problem_disposition.summary: A structured prior-art hunt is needed before custom code gets built: re-problem, blind-parallel multi-source sweep with snowballing, hands-on probing, context-weighted judging, an imperative gate, and a durable record/learn loop -- deja-vu's own ten stages, numbered 0-9 in docs/design.md. No single found candidate covers the whole loop.

candidate_comparisons.summary: The near-match: an 8-stage pipeline (DETECT→…→VERDICT→RECORD), a working stdlib-only scout script hitting GitHub+npm+crates+OpenSSF Scorecard, a 4-verdict model, SPDX license buckets, an ADR template. docs/design.md §6 records this as verified hands-on: the script runs clean, no keys required. Per the §6 comparison table: strong on Trigger, partial on Framing/Sweep/Judge, full on Record; no marks (❤) on Re-problem, Snowball, Probe, Gate, or Learn.

candidate_comparisons.summary: "Search GitHub before answering" — no verdict, no scoring. Per the §6 table: vague on Trigger, no marks on every other stage.

Mature, 31k+-star index for finding installable agent skills — solves a different problem (skill discovery, not prior-art verdicts). Not scored in the §6 table as a whole-loop candidate at all; not a competitor for the full loop, and adopted separately as a manual Sweep lane (see the companion depend-skill-reuse exemplar).

Broader than code (tools, protocols, governance) with confidence-tagged findings, but welded into its own host runtime and not extractable as a standalone loop. Per the §6 table: the only candidate with a full mark anywhere (Judge), partial marks on Re-problem/Trigger/Framing, unclear on Sweep/Gate, no mark on Snowball/Probe/Learn.

"Stop Your AI Agent From Building Tools That Already Exist" — a scan→score→recommend essay with a reuse/adapt/build verdict. Concept only, no implementation to adopt; not scored against the ten-stage table.

uncertainty.residual: of the ten stages (0-9) in docs/design.md §6's comparison table, five have no candidate scoring a full mark: stages 4 (Snowball), 5 (Probe), and 9 (Learn) show no marks at all across all four scored candidates; stages 0 (Re-problem) and 7 (Gate-as-imperative) get at best a partial or unclear mark from one candidate (runx), never a full one. The sweep that produced this table was not exhaustive -- a fuller-coverage skill that wasn't surfaced by the vocabularies tried cannot be ruled out. This packet does not independently verify that a human actually approved the build; it cites docs/design.md's own statement that one did, without an authority receipt to confirm it (this corpus stays at stage: proposed).
uncertainty.confidence: moderate -- the comparison table cites four real, scored candidates plus one essay, and the five-stage gap is real, but the sweep behind that table was not exhaustive and this packet does not independently re-verify each candidate's score; moderate rather than high reflects that residual gap, not doubt about the table's honesty

reversibility: low once shipped and adopted — a multi-stage skill with its own schema, scripts, and evals is not a one-line revert; docs/design.md §6 reports this is why the BUILD verdict was human-gated rather than proceeding on agent authority alone (see uncertainty above on what this packet can and cannot independently confirm about that gating)
